video_generation_spec.title: Earth Obliquity Variation and Synchronized Oscillatory Graph

reproducibility.style: 3D scientific animation with integrated 2D dynamic vector overlays
reproducibility.lighting: Realistic directional sunlight from off-screen left against deep space

scene_layout.background: Deep black space canvas featuring subtle distant starfields and faint nebula dust

left_zone.position: Left third of the frame (x: 15% to 35%, y: 50%)
features: Photorealistic 3D Earth surface with detailed continents and oceanic depth
Fast axial daily rotation along its rotational axis
Continuous back-and-forth nodding/tilting motion (Obliquity variation between 22.5° and 24.5°)
NO text, angle numbers, or height lines on or along the Earth

right_zone.position: Right two-thirds of the frame (x: 35% to 95%, y: 20% to 80%)
right_zone.line_drawing_direction: Glowing blue sinusoidal curve constructed dynamically from right to left, extending towards the Earth

inset_overlay.position: Top-right corner inset box (x: 75% to 92%, y: 10% to 35%)
inset_overlay.style: Semi-transparent rectangular frame with subtle border glow
inset_overlay.motion: Classic mechanical metronome arm swinging steadily back and forth to visually illustrate the periodic nodding/tilting variation mechanism

timeline.action: Deep space environment initializes. Photorealistic 3D Earth appears on the left spinning fast. Scientific plot axes with 'ε (deg)' label fade in on the right.
Earth begins nodding back and forth in obliquity tilt while maintaining fast axial spin. Synchronously, a vibrant blue oscillatory curve draws from right to left toward Earth.

Semi-transparent inset window pops up in the top-right corner showing a metronome swinging back and forth. Earth continues multiple axial tilt oscillations on the left while the blue wave extends towards the globe.
The blue obliquity curve completes its trajectory near Earth. The inset window smoothly fades out as Earth maintains its fast daily spin and ongoing tilting oscillations.

video_generation_spec.text_prompt_for_ai: High-fidelity 16:9 3D scientific animation with 200px render height against a deep space background. On the left third, realistic 3D Earth spinning fast along its axis while smoothly nodding back and forth in obliquity tilt (22.5 to 24.5 degrees) across multiple cycles (clean Earth surface with NO text or angle numbers). On the right two-thirds, a scientific graph rendering a glowing blue oscillatory wave (epsilon tilt angle) from right to left toward Earth. In the top-right corner, an inset overlay showing a mechanical metronome swinging back and forth to demonstrate periodic tilting physics. Smooth 30fps animation.
